newsitem.title: USA: Smith Barney rejigs LatAm model stock portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Smith Barney rejigs LatAm model stock portfolio.

text.p: Smith Barney analyst James Barrineau adjusted his Latin American model stock portfolio Monday, raising Mexico to overweight from neutral and cutting Chile to underweight from overweight.
In an analysis, he also cut Colombia to underweight from neutral and raised Venezuela to neutral from underweight.
"This is a consensus call, but is based in part on proprietary retail funds flow information, which we believe will favor Mexico in the coming months," Barrineau wrote.

"We still feel positive about Chile, but outperformance has run its course and will not be supported by earnings growth. Colombia faces a slow economy, a less favorable interest rate environment and uncertain politics.
"We have been right on Venezuela thus far this year. Macro reforms are positive even if privatizations still flounder."
He added, "It is our feeling that in general Latin equity buyers will rotate over the second half of the year into those markets which have somewhat underperformed others in the first half.
"Thus, in our second weightings change since January, we favor Mexico and Argentina over Chile and Colombia."
Argentina remained overweight in the portfolio.
